paper_title: Stochastic fluctuations of bosonic dark matter
suggested_experiment_name: CASPEr-ZULF Comagnetometer / nEDM / New Force Search
coupling_convention: g_an [GeV^-1], axion-nucleon coupling strength as plotted on y-axis
notes: This paper is a theoretical/methodological study on how to correctly interpret exclusion limits from ultralight bosonic dark matter searches in the T ≪ τ_c regime. It does NOT present new experimental measurements or new exclusion limits. Instead, it demonstrates that previous published constraints from experiments like CASPEr-ZULF, nEDM, and dilaton clock searches were overestimated by factors of 2.7–10 because they incorrectly assumed a fixed field amplitude Φ₀ = Φ_DM rather than accounting for the stochastic Rayleigh distribution of amplitudes. The paper provides correction factors (e.g., γ_stoch/γ_det ≈ 3.0 for scalar couplings, ≈ 8.4 for pseudoscalar with velocity/phase effects) to be applied to existing published limits, but does not extract or report new numerical coupling-vs-mass data points itself. Figures 3 and 4 show corrected exclusion plots, but these are recalculations of prior work, not new measurements. The paper assumes a local DM density of ρ_DM ≈ 0.4 GeV/cm³ (standard halo model), which applies to haloscope-type experiments sensitive to galactic DM.
